
Setup plan: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B (Q4_K_M, 22.1 GB) with Ollama, tuned settings
  runtime chosen: no runtime gives a working setup with these settings; simulating anyway (try a smaller model or --ctx)
  context 65536 tokens · 16-bit context cache · serves at http://127.0.0.1:11434 as "qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm"
  expected: first reply 16 s, then ~11 s per turn, writing at 33 tok/s
  ✓ Codex CLI connects through `cyrlm bridge`, which passes its requests to Ollama's Chat Completions API at http://127.0.0.1:11434 as model qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm.

Nothing has been run. Run each step yourself (or let your coding agent run them, with your approval):

1. Check what is already installed
   cyrlm did not find Ollama. These read-only commands confirm what is installed and running, and that there is room for the 22.1 GB download. A failing version command means the runtime is not installed or not on PATH.
     ollama --version
     curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/version
     codex --version
     df -h "$HOME"

2. Install Ollama  [needs admin]
   Official install script: installs /usr/local/bin/ollama (with CUDA/ROCm libraries when it finds a GPU) and an `ollama` systemd service that starts the server on port 11434. It uses sudo.
     curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh

3. Download Qwen3.6 35B-A3B Q4_K_M (22.1 GB)  [downloads 22.1 GB]
   Pulls the exact Q4_K_M GGUF from Hugging Face (unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF) — the file cyrlm's prediction is based on. If Ollama reports an unsupported architecture for this file, use the library build instead: `ollama pull qwen3.6:35b-a3b`.
     ollama pull hf.co/unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_M

4. Create qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm with a 65536-token context
   Ollama's default context depends on GPU memory (often 4096 tokens) and the OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible APIs cannot change it per request; a Modelfile with num_ctx fixes it for this model only. The new model shares the downloaded weights (no extra disk). Use qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm as the model name in your harness.
     ollama create qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm -f "$HOME/.cyrlm/ollama/qwen3.6-35b-a3b-cyrlm.Modelfile"
   Create ~/.cyrlm/ollama/qwen3.6-35b-a3b-cyrlm.Modelfile:
     # Generated by cyrlm plan: Qwen3.6 35B-A3B Q4_K_M on Ollama.
     FROM hf.co/unsloth/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-GGUF:UD-Q4_K_M
     PARAMETER num_ctx 65536

5. Set Ollama server settings: OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1  [needs admin]
   Server-wide settings for never unload the model when idle (default: 5 minutes, after which the next request reloads it and re-processes the whole prompt). Ollama reads them only from the server's environment at start-up, so they are set persistently and the server is restarted. Running models are unloaded by the restart. This writes a systemd drop-in (same effect as `sudo systemctl edit ollama`) for the service the install script created. If you run `ollama serve` yourself, export the variables in that shell instead.
     sudo mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d
     printf '%s\n' '[Service]' 'Environment="OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1"' | sudo tee /etc/systemd/system/ollama.service.d/cyrlm.conf >/dev/null
     sudo systemctl daemon-reload
     sudo systemctl restart ollama
   then restart: Ollama server (this step restarts it)

6. Load qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm and check GPU placement
   Preloads the model so the first harness request does not pay the load time. In `ollama ps`, CONTEXT should read 65536 and PROCESSOR should read 100% GPU (anything else means part of the model runs on the CPU and will be much slower than predicted).
     curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/generate -d '{"model": "qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm"}' >/dev/null
     ollama ps

7. Start the Codex CLI bridge
   Codex sends requests that local runtimes' own Responses endpoints do not fully handle (namespaced tools, several developer messages, hosted web search; llama.cpp skips namespace tools and strict chat templates reject a second system message). `cyrlm bridge` accepts Codex CLI's requests on port 11535 (or the next free port) and passes them to http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions, the runtime's most mature API, with system messages merged for the model's chat template and tool calls mapped back; runtime errors are shown in Codex CLI instead of being retried. It returns once it answers and prints the exact Codex CLI command.
     cyrlm bridge --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:11434 --model qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm --harness codex --ctx 65536 --background

8. Start Codex CLI with qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm
   Everything is passed with -c overrides, so no Codex config file is edited, plain `codex` keeps working as before, and nothing depends on Codex's config layout (profiles moved to separate files in 0.134). Use the command the bridge printed: it has the real port and, when codex is not on your terminal's PATH, its full path. Web search is off because a local model cannot run OpenAI's hosted search.
     /Applications/ChatGPT.app/Contents/Resources/codex-cli/CodexCLI.app/Contents/MacOS/codex -c model_providers.cyrlm.name=cyrlm -c model_providers.cyrlm.base_url=http://127.0.0.1:11535/v1 -c model_providers.cyrlm.wire_api=responses -c model_provider=cyrlm -c web_search=disabled -c model_context_window=65536 -c model_auto_compact_token_limit=52428 -m qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm
   then restart: Codex CLI: start a new session in your own terminal

9. Verify the setup
   Checks that Ollama answers at http://127.0.0.1:11434 with qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm, that the context window is 65536 tokens and compares real speed with cyrlm's prediction. It then sends requests in codex's own format (a greeting, a tool call and the tool result) and reports "Ready" only if all three work: a fast runtime can still reject a coding tool's requests. The setup is not done until this says Ready.
     cyrlm verify --runtime ollama --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:11434 --model qwen3.6:35b-a3b-cyrlm --catalog-model qwen3.6-35b-a3b --quant Q4_K_M --ctx 65536 --harness codex

⚠ Restarting the Ollama service unloads any running models.
⚠ These steps need administrator rights (sudo): Install Ollama; Set Ollama server settings: OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE=-1.
⚠ The model download is 22.1 GB; keep at least 26.3 GB of disk space free.
